# Crew API: consent (Owner endpoints)

Part of the [Crew API reference](README.md).

## GET /v1/crew/owner/grant-requests

List grant requests waiting for consent.

| About | This endpoint |
|---|---|
| Status | Available now: owner only |
| Tier | Owner |
| Stability | stable |
| Callers the API defines | The owner, with the owner's own sign-in. |

Lists the requests apps made through local authorization (GET /oauth/authorize) that wait for the host owner's consent, oldest first. The host owner's credential is required; authenticated remote access is allowed. Shared Crew teammates (relay, SSM guests and tailnet collaborators) and app tokens receive 403 owner_only. Host-owner-only listing protects which local apps requested access; the RFC's rule that the Owner tier is for the owner only requires it. No consent page is required.

Request headers:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Crew-API-Version` | string | no | The minor version the client was written for. Without it, the server answers with 1.0 behaviour. The server never refuses a request because this version is old. |
| `X-Request-Id` | string | no | A caller may supply its own; an id assigned by an intermediary in front of the gateway wins. |

Response `200`: The grant requests.

Response headers:

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `X-Request-Id` | string | One id per request, supplied by the caller or an intermediary, or generated by the gateway. Also written to the audit log and the error body. |
| `Crew-API-Version` | string | The server's minor version, for example 1.3. |

Response body fields (`application/json`), [GrantRequestList](schemas.md#grantrequestlist):

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | `list` | yes |  |
| `data` | array of [GrantRequest](schemas.md#grantrequest) | yes |  |
| `first_id` | string or null | no |  |
| `last_id` | string or null | no |  |
| `has_more` | boolean | yes |  |

Errors. The response body is [Error](schemas.md#error); its `error.code` field holds the code.

| Status | Codes | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | `invalid_token`, `stale_session_reauth` | 401: invalid_token, stale_session_reauth. For the Owner tier: no quota headers. |
| 403 | `owner_only` | 403: owner_only. A delegated credential, an embed credential, a local app token and a dashboard session that is not the owner's all get this on the Owner tier; /v1 does not hide routes behind 404. |
| 500 | `internal_error` | 500: internal_error. For embed-credential endpoints: no quota headers. |
| 503 | `instance_unavailable` | 503: instance_unavailable. For embed-credential endpoints: no quota headers. |

## GET /v1/crew/owner/grant-requests/{request_id}

Read one grant request.

| About | This endpoint |
|---|---|
| Status | Available now: owner only |
| Tier | Owner |
| Stability | stable |
| Callers the API defines | The owner, with the owner's own sign-in. |

Returns one grant request by its id, answered or not, so the owner can see how it was answered and which grant it led to (amendment, proposed). The request stays readable until it and its authorization code have expired, or for as long as the grant it led to exists; after that it is 404. The host owner's credential is required; Shared Crew teammates and app tokens receive 403 owner_only.

Path parameters:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `request_id` | string | yes | greq_ id |

Request headers:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Crew-API-Version` | string | no | The minor version the client was written for. Without it, the server answers with 1.0 behaviour. The server never refuses a request because this version is old. |
| `X-Request-Id` | string | no | A caller may supply its own; an id assigned by an intermediary in front of the gateway wins. |

Response `200`: The request.

Response headers:

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `X-Request-Id` | string | One id per request, supplied by the caller or an intermediary, or generated by the gateway. Also written to the audit log and the error body. |
| `Crew-API-Version` | string | The server's minor version, for example 1.3. |

Response body fields (`application/json`), [GrantRequest](schemas.md#grantrequest):

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes |  |
| `object` | `grant_request` | yes |  |
| `namespace` | `default` | yes | The group this record belongs to. Stored on every record; today it has one fixed value. |
| `status` | [GrantRequestStatus](schemas.md#grantrequeststatus) | yes |  |
| `client_id` | string | yes | As the app reported it |
| `client_name` | string | no | As the app reported it; the first 80 characters of client_id when the app sent none |
| `verified` | `false` | no | Always false: a program on this machine reported the name and client_id, and nothing verified them |
| `redirect_uri` | string (uri) | no | The loopback address the authorization code goes to |
| `user_code` | string | no | Short code the app shows, so the owner can tell which request is which |
| `requested_scopes` | array of string | yes |  |
| `requested_bots` | array of string | no | The Bot names the app sends as the repeated bots query parameter of GET /oauth/authorize, one Bot per occurrence, without splitting; empty when omitted. The app is expected to send the exact model id from GET /v1/models. Names follow kiro_crew.members.is_dispatchable_member_name with the MEMBER_NAME_MAX_CHARS length limit; duplicates are refused. Asking checks format, never existence. Malformed bots gives 400 invalid_request even with an invalid scope. Asking again requires the same bots values in the same order. MAX_REQUESTED_BOTS is the chosen bound for one request and one decision, set equal to crew_teams.TEAM_MEMBERS_MAX (500), the largest Bot list the product keeps elsewhere. The request must fit aiohttp's 8190-byte request line. The decision body must fit 4 KiB (_BODY_MAX); a bots list that does not fit gives 400 invalid_request, and the owner gives a shorter list. |
| `created_at` | [Timestamp](schemas.md#timestamp) | yes | Unix seconds. |
| `expires_at` | [Timestamp](schemas.md#timestamp) | yes | Unix seconds. |
| `decided_at` | integer or null | no | When the owner answered (amendment, proposed) |
| `decided_by` | object or null | no | Who answered: the kind of caller, never a token (amendment, proposed) |
| `granted_scopes` | array of string | no | Only when approved; what the owner gave, which may be fewer than requested (amendment, proposed) |
| `granted_bots` | array of string | no | Only when approved; the Bot names the owner gave, which may be none. They become the grant's bots with mode selected. Names follow kiro_crew.members.is_dispatchable_member_name and MEMBER_NAME_MAX_CHARS, with no duplicates. MAX_REQUESTED_BOTS is the chosen bound for one request and one decision, set equal to crew_teams.TEAM_MEMBERS_MAX (500), the largest Bot list the product keeps elsewhere. The decision body must fit 4 KiB (_BODY_MAX); a bots list that does not fit gives 400 invalid_request, and the owner gives a shorter list. The decision checks expiry, pending status and the requested subset before reading the roster. The grants list returns the owner's recorded selection; no route enforces it yet. |
| `grant_id` | string or null | no | The grant this request led to, set once the app redeemed its code (amendment, proposed) |

Errors. The response body is [Error](schemas.md#error); its `error.code` field holds the code.

| Status | Codes | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | `invalid_token`, `stale_session_reauth` | 401: invalid_token, stale_session_reauth. For the Owner tier: no quota headers. |
| 403 | `owner_only` | 403: owner_only. A delegated credential, an embed credential, a local app token and a dashboard session that is not the owner's all get this on the Owner tier; /v1 does not hide routes behind 404. |
| 404 | `not_found`, `model_not_found` | 404: not_found, model_not_found. For embed-credential endpoints: no quota headers. |
| 500 | `internal_error` | 500: internal_error. For embed-credential endpoints: no quota headers. |
| 503 | `instance_unavailable` | 503: instance_unavailable. For embed-credential endpoints: no quota headers. |

## POST /v1/crew/owner/grant-requests/{request_id}/decision

Approve or deny a grant request.

| About | This endpoint |
|---|---|
| Status | Available now: owner only |
| Tier | Owner |
| Stability | stable |
| Callers the API defines | The owner, with the owner's own sign-in. |

The host owner's answer to one grant request. An approval may narrow the requested scopes and never widens them. Only after an approval does the app's next GET /oauth/authorize redirect with a code. The host owner's credential is required; authenticated remote access is allowed. Shared Crew teammates (relay, SSM guests and tailnet collaborators) and app tokens receive 403 owner_only. Host-owner-only consent prevents issuing a local credential that outlives a teammate's access; the RFC's rule that the Owner tier is for the owner only requires it.

Path parameters:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `request_id` | string | yes | greq_ id |

Request headers:

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Crew-API-Version` | string | no | The minor version the client was written for. Without it, the server answers with 1.0 behaviour. The server never refuses a request because this version is old. |
| `X-Request-Id` | string | no | A caller may supply its own; an id assigned by an intermediary in front of the gateway wins. |

Request body fields (`application/json`), [GrantRequestDecision](schemas.md#grantrequestdecision):

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `decision` | `approve`, `deny` | yes |  |
| `scopes` | array of string | no | Only with approve: the scopes to give. Must be a subset of requested_scopes. Left out: all requested scopes. |
| `bots` | array of string | no | Only with approve: a JSON array of exact Bot names from GET /v1/models, a subset of requested_bots. Names follow kiro_crew.members.is_dispatchable_member_name and MEMBER_NAME_MAX_CHARS, with no duplicates. MAX_REQUESTED_BOTS is the chosen bound for one request and one decision, set equal to crew_teams.TEAM_MEMBERS_MAX (500), the largest Bot list the product keeps elsewhere. The decision body must fit 4 KiB (_BODY_MAX); a bots list that does not fit gives 400 invalid_request, and the owner gives a shorter list. After the body's size, decision and scopes form (each 400 invalid_request), the handler checks the request before any Bot check (404 not_found if unknown or expired, 409 grant_request_already_resolved if answered), then the requested subset, then the roster. Each Bot must exist in that read. When an approval gives at least one Bot, unreadable configuration or a degraded Bot roster gives 503 instance_unavailable without recording a decision. An approval that gives none, and a deny, do not read the roster. Asking via GET /oauth/authorize uses repeated bots query parameters, one Bot per occurrence, and checks format only, never existence; asking again requires the same values in the same order. Left out: no Bot, because a Bot is never given by default. Explicit null gives 400 invalid_request (bots must be a list of strings). On a deny, the server ignores bots whatever its value, even though the schema declares an array. |

Response `200`: The grant request after the decision.

Response headers:

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `X-Request-Id` | string | One id per request, supplied by the caller or an intermediary, or generated by the gateway. Also written to the audit log and the error body. |
| `Crew-API-Version` | string | The server's minor version, for example 1.3. |
